result.rationale: The server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is only z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine, and addGuests.handler.ts filters existing attendees with exact case-sensitive equality (guest === attendee.email) and never deduplicates within the `guests` array before createMany. So duplicate or differently-cased emails can create duplicate attendee rows, exactly as the finding describes; uniqueness is enforced only in the client dialog's local zod schema.

judged_text: Server-side dedup only filters guests matching existing attendees by exact case-sensitive string equality and never deduplicates within the `guests` array itself; the uniqueness rule exists only in the client dialog's local zod schema. A direct tRPC call submitting the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows in one createMany; submitting an already-invited email with different casing ('User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com') creates a duplicate attendee record that also receives a second calendar invite.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Server-side dedup only filters guests matching existing attendees by exact case-sensitive string equality and never deduplicates within the `guests` array itself; the uniqueness rule exists only in the client dialog's local zod schema. A direct tRPC call submitting the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows in one createMany; submitting an already-invited email with different casing ('User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com') creates a duplicate attendee record that also receives a second calendar invite.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, server-side filtering only excludes existing attendees via exact, case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not deduplicate within the incoming `guests` array before `attendees.createMany` (it uses `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` which preserves duplicates from `guests`). The tRPC input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also lacks a uniqueness refinement. Therefore a direct tRPC call can submit duplicate emails (or case-variants of an existing attendee) and the handler will attempt to create duplicate attendee rows and then call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` / `sendAddGuestsEmails` with those duplicates.
